summary: Wrote a 5-phase plan covering all six dispatch goals: a home.activation enforced-key jq step in modules/home/services/sf1-hub-ben.nix declaring coalesce_s=300/net_timeout_s=15/deadline_s=20, a notify-only systemd-user watch timer for fail-closed markers, convergence of both attached checkouts via switch, a sendable upstream defect write-up, and a docs/sf1-hub.md update. Premise re-validation corrected three dispatch figures: only 3 of the 38 blocks are initiating suspension events, so the per-round-trip failure rate is ~0.17%, not ~2%, and the ~50-action survival estimate is wrong. Found a second, unflagged fail-closed surface not in the dispatch or the research report: guard.py send()'s breaker.json is open in BOTH checkouts since 2026-11-14/15 with 191 commit events stranded in outbox/, so the consented hub_commit_events reporting has been silently dead for days; scope extended to cover it in the write-up, the attach calculus, and the watch surface.

artifacts.summary: 5-phase plan: guard knob activation step, fail-closed marker watch timer, apply/converge both checkouts, two-surface upstream defect write-up, docs/sf1-hub.md update.

user_decision.question: Both attached checkouts' sender breakers have been open since 2026-11-14/15 with roughly 191 commit events stranded in outbox/; running `guard.py send --reset` would immediately deliver several days of queued commit metadata to Oliver's hosted sink. Who runs that reset, and when?
options: Leave both breakers open; the plan records the counts and the exact reset command per checkout, and you run it yourself when ready
Reset both breakers during the implement phase and let the queued events drain unattended
Leave them open pending the conversation with Oliver about whether a days-late burst is wanted at all
user_decision.recommended: Leave both breakers open; the plan records the counts and the exact reset command per checkout, and you run it yourself when ready
user_decision.obligation: Restores the hub_commit_events reporting consented in CONSENT-benjamin.json without an agent performing an outward-facing, irreversible delivery of several days of commit metadata unattended; Phase 3's record must name the stranded count and the exact reset command per checkout for the obligation to be discharged.
